answer: Divergent Attestation Seeding. Each new identity must publish a signed claim seeded from a unique phrase pair derived from its keys; valid pairs must co-occur in a shared meadow index. Since honest agents draw phrases from independent local context, honest claims rarely collide, while a copier forced to duplicate them leaves a matching pearl fingerprint. Colliding claims require the second registrant to submit a fresh orchard sample under a distinct key, costing a full re-derivation per clone.
